holidays.name: World UFO Day
holidays.description: A day for gazing skyward and talking about unidentified flying objects, extraterrestrial visitors, and whether we are alone in the universe. Enthusiasts hold watch parties, share sighting stories, and wear tinfoil with pride.
holidays.origin: Organized by the World UFO Day group, which chose July 2 to commemorate the reported 1947 Roswell incident. A rival organization promotes June 24 instead, so UFO fans can't even agree on the date.
holidays.funFact: Two different dates compete for World UFO Day: July 2 (Roswell) and June 24 (the anniversary of Kenneth Arnold's 1947 sighting), meaning some fans celebrate twice.

holidays.name: I Forgot Day
holidays.description: A day to forgive yourself and others for forgetting things, from birthdays to anniversaries to why you walked into the room. Nobody is allowed to scold you for forgetting, assuming you remember to celebrate.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, lighthearted observance that has circulated in quirky holiday calendars. It reportedly exists to give forgetful people a free pass, though no one seems to recall who started it.
holidays.funFact: The day is appropriately easy to miss, and many people who observe it admit they only remembered it after it was over.

holidays.name: World Sports Journalists Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the reporters, commentators, photographers, and writers who bring game-day drama to fans around the globe, from last-second buzzer beaters to epic penalty shootouts.
holidays.origin: Established by the International Sports Press Association (AIPS), which was founded in 1924 around the Paris Olympics. The day recognizes the contribution of sports media to the world.
holidays.funFact: AIPS now represents thousands of sports journalists in over 150 countries.

holidays.name: National Anisette Day
holidays.description: A toast to the licorice-flavored liqueur flavored with anise seed, beloved in Mediterranean countries. It's sipped neat, splashed in coffee, or poured over ice for those who love black jelly beans.
holidays.origin: A food and drink observance that emerged from the unofficial holiday calendar, celebrating anise-flavored spirits that have been enjoyed since ancient times.
holidays.funFact: Anise-flavored drinks appear under many names around the world, including ouzo in Greece, sambuca in Italy, pastis in France, and arak in the Levant.

holidays.name: National Made in the USA Day
holidays.description: A day to hunt through your closet and kitchen for products stamped with American manufacturing pride, and perhaps to be surprised by how few you can find.
holidays.origin: A patriotic consumer observance placed just before Independence Day to encourage shopping for domestically manufactured goods and supporting American workers.
holidays.funFact: Under Federal Trade Commission rules, a product labeled 'Made in USA' must be 'all or virtually all' made in the United States.
